### Method 1: Direct Proportion
We know that the recipe makes 24 cookies with 3 cups of flour. We want to find out how many cups of flour are needed to make 144 cookies. We can set up a proportion to solve this:

\[
\frac{24 \text{ cookies}}{3 \text{ cups of flour}} = \frac{144 \text{ cookies}}{x \text{ cups of flour}}
\]

\[
24x = 3 \times 144
\]

\[

\]

\[
x = \frac{432}{24}
\]

\[
x = 18
\]

So, the baker will need 18 cups of flour to make 144 cookies.

### Method 2: Scaling Up
We can also scale up the recipe directly. Since the recipe makes 24 cookies, we need to determine how many times larger 144 cookies is compared to 24 cookies:

\[
\frac{144 \text{ cookies}}{24 \text{ cookies}} = 6
\]

This means we need 6 times the amount of flour. Since the original recipe calls for 3 cups of flour, we multiply by 6:

\[
3 \text{ cups} \times 6 = 18 \text{ cups}
\]

### Method 3: Using Ratios
We can also use the ratio of cookies to flour directly. The ratio of cookies to flour in the original recipe is:

\[
\frac{24 \text{ cookies}}{3 \text{ cups of flour}} = 8 \text{ cookies per cup of flour}
\]

To find out how many cups of flour are needed for 144 cookies, we set up the following ratio:

\frac{144 \text{ cookies}}{x \text{ cups of flour}} = 8 \text{ cookies per cup of flour}
\]

\]

\[

\]

\[
x = 18
\]

So, the baker will need 18 cups of flour to make 144 cookies.
